newsitem.title: POLAND: Merrill values Polish KGHM at $1.1-1.3 bln -paper.
newsitem.headline: Merrill values Polish KGHM at $1.1-1.3 bln -paper.

text.p: Polish copper concern KGHM Polska Miedz SA, due for flotation in London and Warsaw in early July, is worth between $1.1 and $1.3 billion, Merrill Lynch said in a report.

Rzeczpospolita business daily on Wednesday quoted Merrill Lynch research report putting KGHM's price to earning ratio (P/E) at 8-10 in 1997 given that the copper giant's subsidiary firms were worth $152 million.
Merrill said it expected KGHM's production costs to fall to $1,435 per tonne in the year 2000 from $1,943 at present.
It said that KGHM planned to invest some $2.5 billion within five years to reduce costs, increase output and modernise production.
According to Merrill data wages accounted for 33 percent of of the copper maker's costs in 1996, materials, energy and fuel for 34 percent and repairs for seven percent.

KGHM's copper-ore deposists amount to 922 million tonnes, which were capable of yielding 15.6 million tonnes of copper, enough to keep the concern's three mines producing for 24, 34 and 39 years respectively, the report said.
In 1996 some 36 percent of KGHM's copper output was sold domestically, France and Germany accounted for 14 percent each, seven percent was sold to the United Kingdom and six to Hungary.
NOTE - Results given by KGHM and forecasts by Merrill Lynch, which along with Robert Fleming investment bank is the co-manager of KGHM's upcomming flotation.
